_doc: The endings of the endings_1 pack (docs/CONTENT.md section 13). id, title, epilogue (4 to 8 sentences, shown on the ending screen) and base_score (the ending's base points; the score maths adds credits, crew, POIs and landmarks).

endings.title: Halcyon, Quietly
endings.epilogue: The Halcyon council gives you a berth, a bell and a bowl of something green, in that order. You are the first visitor in forty years who did not ask for anything, and they find this so confusing that they ask you to stay a week, then a season. Your crew take over a terrace, and your engineer is offered a classroom and a child who has never seen a wrench and cannot stop asking what it is for. Somebody paints your ship's name on a lamp and hangs it at the edge of the Reach, so the next lost thing will know where the light is. On clear nights the loop still plays on every channel, a forty-second sentence started late by a different thumb each time. Once in a while the thumb is yours.

endings.title: The Convoy to the Lamps
endings.epilogue: It takes a season to organise and one afternoon to leave, and the Drift has never seen anything like it: barges, cutters, a Prism unfolding like a flower, and a floating laundry nobody can explain. Halcyon had a plan for visitors, and the plan lasts about four minutes, after which it is a party. The gates are not taken. They are shared, with the ceremonial gravity of a thing that has only ever belonged to one family, and nobody has said so out loud yet, but they are going to need a lot more chairs. Behind you the Drift is a little emptier and a little less alone. Ma Gantry stands in a terrace garden, scandalised by the price of tomatoes, which is zero. She charges the first harvest anyway. You cannot stop a person being themselves, and out here, finally, you would not want to.

endings.title: All Well, Crew All Present
endings.epilogue: The airlock opens before you knock. It is warm inside, and everything is exactly on time. The lamps are lit and the beds are made, and the soup is the best you have ever tasted, and nobody asks where you are from. Your crew sit down at a table laid for exactly the right number, and for a while it is wonderful. The flight recorder makes a new entry every morning at six, and it never changes: ALL WELL, CREW ALL PRESENT. At some point you stop noticing who is counting, and at some point after that you stop minding. The loop still plays from every window, and its last line has changed. It says, We kept a lamp on for you, and it is your voice.

endings.title: Restoration, In Triplicate
endings.epilogue: Director Vasko files the Restoration notice in triplicate, and the Lattice comes back to the Drift with a stamp. The first ship through is a Concord cutter, because of course it is, and the second is a Scrapper barge, because of course it is. The third is Hallett, who has brought his mug. The gates come on one by one, each with a small pause while a clerk checks that it is allowed. It is slow, it is marvellous, and nobody can say a word against the forms now, because the forms worked. They give you a certificate of exceptional service, in triplicate, which is the best thing anyone has ever given you, and you are going to be unbearable about it.

endings.title: The Free Gate
endings.epilogue: The Free Gate opens with a bang that bends the nearest three ships and wakes the Good Wrench. Ma Gantry declares it open to all, at her usual rates. Within the hour there are forty toll booths, a customs shed, a bar, a second bar, and a cousin selling maps of the other side to people who have not been there. It is loud and crooked and held together with welds, and it works. Rustfangs and Concord queue at the same airlock and trade insults through the same hatch, and the Concord files a complaint, and Ma frames it. They give you the Good Wrench. It is, in fact, not that good, and it is the best thing you have ever owned.

endings.title: Somewhere New
endings.epilogue: The Lumen do not restart the gate. They ask it a question, in the fourth note, and it answers by opening somewhere new. Through the door is a sky with the wrong number of stars: you count three thousand and twelve, and then you lose count, on purpose. Nobody knows where it leads, and that is the best part. The Lumen send a small, delighted skiff to find out, and it comes back with a plant nobody can name and a message that is just the fourth note, in a voice that has a mouth. You are allowed to be the first to look. You are also allowed to come back, which is rarer, and which they note in the margin with great interest.

endings.title: Visitors: One
endings.epilogue: The soup is the best soup you have ever had, which is the gate trying very hard. When the meal is over the chairs are pushed back all at once, the way people stand up when the shift ends, and eleven tired people in work jackets say thank you, and sorry it took so long, and walk out through the door that has been held open for forty years. It takes eleven seconds, and after that the green lights go out along the lane, one by one, like a street at dawn, and the Hollow drift home with their kettles still warm. The recorder prints one last line: ALL WELL. CREW: ALL PRESENT. VISITORS: ONE. THANK YOU. Then the gate closes, properly, for the first time since the Snap, and for the first time in forty years it does not feel like a held breath.

endings.title: A Hook for Your Helmet
endings.epilogue: You hang your helmet on the hook. It fits. The berth has a window onto the whole slow turning of the Rusthold, and a chair that does not fold, and a kettle on the shelf, because Ma sent one over with a straight face. In the mornings the dock hands wave at you with their welding masks pushed up. In the evenings somebody brings you a wrench to look at, and you say you are retired, and look at it anyway. Your old crew send postcards from places you did not know had post. Ma comes by on Thursdays and says nothing about the night the Rusthold went quiet, and charges you for the tea.
